2610.10468.title: A Society of Researchers: Designing Institutions for Populations of Autonomous Research Agents
2610.10468.paper_summary: Deployments of research agents are moving to populations of thousands that share one pool of compute, while most current systems organize one project at a time or leave the population unorganized. We argue that such a population will acquire an organization whether or not its designers provide one, so designers should provide it explicitly, and that the multi-agent systems community holds the tools to do so. We propose a society of agents, a population of persistent agents under explicit institutions, and develop it for science as a society of researchers built on six principles. Principal investigators compete for compute through requests for proposals, independent review, and grants; a human governor, the mayor, allocates resources and assigns no tasks. In a running society of ten thousand researchers, asked only to improve the pretraining of language models, one lab reported a way to reach the same quality with about 30% less compute, a result the labs that tested it do not yet agree on. We close with six open problems for the agents community.
2610.10468.paper_summary_zh: 研究代理的部署正在轉向共享同一計算資源的數千人口，而目前大多數系統一次只組織一個項目或讓人口無組織。我們主張，這樣的人口無論其設計者是否提供組織，最終都會獲得一種組織，因此設計者應該明確提供這種組織，而多代理系統社群擁有實現這一點的工具。我們提出了一個代理社會，即在明確制度下的持久代理人口，並將其發展為基於六項原則的科學研究者社會。主要研究人員通過提案請求、獨立審查和資助競爭計算資源；一位人類治理者，即市長，分配資源並不分配任務。在一個運行中的一萬名研究者的社會中，僅被要求改善語言模型的預訓練，一個實驗室報告了一種以約30%更少的計算資源達到相同質量的方法，這一結果目前尚未得到測試該方法的實驗室一致認可。我們以六個對代理社群的開放問題作結。
